lead: Minneapolis plumbing is built for deep cold, deep frost and older homes with basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Minneapolis.
risk: frozen pipes and water service lines, basement plumbing and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, basements and old pipes
why: Many Minneapolis homes were built before 1940, with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in some cases. Almost every house has a basement with the water heater, floor drain and laundry.
Long, deep winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and can freeze water service lines when frost goes deep. Spring snowmelt fills sump pits and tests basement drainage.
utility: Minneapolis Public Works, Water Treatment and Distribution
water: Minneapolis draws its water from the Mississippi River and treats it, including softening. Many older homes still have lead service lines, and the city has a program to replace them.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Ask the city about your service line material.
Test your sump pump before spring thaw.
areas: PipeMend works in Uptown, Northeast, Longfellow, Nokomis, North Minneapolis, Downtown, Southwest and every other Minneapolis neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Minneapolis, and plumbers must be licensed by the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry.

faq.q: What should I do if my water service line freezes in Minneapolis?
faq.a: Call a plumber; frozen service lines usually need special thawing equipment. Keep a faucet open, never use an open flame, and contact the city's water department if the freeze may be on the public side.
